Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Gym injury one week prior.
Comparison: [REDACTED].

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Femorotibial alignment is anatomic. Avulsive fragmentation of inferior patellar enthesophytes with some reactive marrow edema in the inferior patella. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: Irregularity of the distal quadriceps tendon, most likely sequelae of laxity due to patella alta, possibly with some mild underlying tendinosis.
Patella tendon: Complete rupture of the proximal patellar tendon with 1.5-2 cm retracted tendon gap and intervening fluid/hematoma formation. Underlying severe patellar tendinosis. Osseous fragments are embedded within the retracted patellar tendon fibers.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: Posttraumatic edema in Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. Significant patella alta due to the patellar tendon rupture. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 15 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
Grade 1 strain of the distal vastus lateralis. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
Extensive posttraumatic soft tissue edema about the knee with moderate prepatellar bursitis. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Complete, retracted rupture of the proximal patellar tendon with associated avulsive fragmentation of inferior patellar enthesophytes.
2.	Extensive posttraumatic soft tissue about the knee with moderate prepatellar bursitis.

Right knee MRI:

INDICATION: Right knee pain since 4 months refractory to physical therapy. Posterior knee pain.

COMPARISON: Compared to right knee radiographs from [Date].

FINDINGS:
Mild synovitis. Small debris is in the suprapatellar recess and mild effusion. 4.5 x 2.4 x 0.9 cm Baker's cyst.

ANTERIOR COMPARTMENT:
Mild to moderate chondrosis with a focal full-thickness fissure with subchondral bone change at the medial aspect of the lateral patellar facet. Intact extensor mechanism. No significant edema within Hoffa's fat pad.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Moderate chondrosis with area of more than 50% thinning of cartilage. Small medial meniscal body undersurface tear with a flipped fragment in the medial aspect of the medial tibial plateau measuring 7 x 2 mm. Radial tear involving the posterior horn with a flipped fragment towards the intercondylar notch. This fragment measure 8 x 4 mm. Prior healed traumatic injury to the medial collateral ligament proximal attachment.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Mild chondrosis. No discrete meniscal tear. Curvilinear bony fragment overlying the posterior aspect of the fibular head most likely related to a prior avulsion injury of arcuate ligament or fabellofibular ligament. Lateral collateral ligament and biceps femoris appear intact. Iliotibial band appears slightly thickened but without surrounding edema, nonspecific.

INTERCONDYLAR COMPARTMENT:
Anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament are intact.

IMPRESSION:
1. Moderate medial compartment chondrosis with complex meniscal tear described above with a flipped fragment medially to the medial tibial plateau and posterior horn flipped fragment near the intercondylar notch.
2. Mild to moderate chondrosis involving the anterior and lateral compartment. Mild synovitis with debris is in the suprapatellar recess.
3. Remote avulsion injury at the proximal medial collateral ligament and fibular head.

FINDINGS:

Fluid:
Small joint effusion. No Bakers cyst. Small ganglion cyst associated with the medial head gastrocnemius insertion.

Medial compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament, cartilage):
Degenerative multidirectional tear, with longitudinal horizontal tear at the junction of the body and posterior horn, and radial tear of the posterior horn. There is mild meniscal extrusion. Full-thickness chondral loss at the medial femoral condyle, with diffuse high-grade medial articular cartilage thinning. Small marginal osteophytes in keeping with mild medial compartment osteoarthrosis.
Thickening of the MCL with mild overlying edema in keeping with grade 1 injury.

Lateral compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament complex, cartilage):
Blunting of the inner free edge of the body of the lateral meniscus in keeping with a small partial radial tear, on a background of degenerative signal changes. Mild partial-thickness chondral thinning of lateral articular cartilage.
Normal lateral collateral ligament structures. Trace of fluid within the popliteal recess.

Intercondylar compartment (anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments):
Mucoid degeneration of the ACL, with early ganglion cyst formation within the distal insertion. Normal PCL.

Anterior compartment (extensor mechanism, cartilage, Hoffa's fat pad):
Normal extensor mechanism. Normal fat pads.
Full-thickness cartilage loss at the medial patellar articular facet with mild subchondral reactive edema.
Small marginal osteophytes in keeping with mild osteoarthrosis.

Bones:
Normal.

Muscles and neurovascular structures:
Normal.

Other findings:
None

CONCLUSION:
1.Tricompartmental osteoarthrosis/chondropathy as detailed above.
2.Degenerative multidirectional medial meniscal tear with mild meniscal extrusion.
3.Small lateral meniscal partial radial tear.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Left knee pain for one month. No known injury. No history of surgery.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture. Normal background marrow signal. No focal osseous lesion. Irregular exostosis at the posterior medial tibial plateau with associated thin T2 hyperintense cartilaginous lining, compatible with an osteochondroma.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. Small multiloculated Baker's cyst with internal debris.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Probable small oblique undersurface tear at the posterior horn without extrusion.
Medial compartment cartilage: Intact.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: No tear.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Low-grade articular cartilage loss at the posterior lateral femoral condyle.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Intact.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): No tear.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): No tear.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Extensor Apparatus: Normal quadriceps tendon. Normal patellar tendon.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance is 11 mm, normal.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No disproportionate muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Trace pes anserinus bursitis. Small ganglion cyst at the posterior lateral knee, in the region of the proximal popliteus tendon sheath. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Probable small oblique undersurface tear at the posterior horn of the medial meniscus without extrusion. 
2.	Small left knee effusion with a small multiloculated Baker's cyst.
3.	Mild pes anserinus bursitis.
4.	Osteochondroma along the posteromedial tibia.

MRI of right Knee with 
-Locator, SG PD FatSat, SG T2W FS, SG T1W, CO T2W FS, AX T2W FS

> The contour of ACL is not in a straight line and increase signal intensity inside, in favor of tear.
> Slight increased signal intensity of PCL on T1WI and F/S T2WI, R/O grade 1 injury.
 > Joint effusion and suprapatellar bursitis with suprapatellar and medial and lateral plicae; hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis.
 > Ill-defined bone marrow edema in posterior aspect of tibial plateau with slight depressed contour, in favor of bone contusion with R/O occult subchondral fracture.
> There are linear signal intensity in posterior horn of medial meniscus and lateral meniscus, without significant extending into the surface, R/O degeneration.
> Heterogenous signal intensity of articular cartilage and focal thin cartilage at odd facet, in favor of grade 2-3 patellar chondromalacia.
> Mild fat stranding along medial collateral ligament, R/O grade 1 injury.
> Spur formation of knee joint
> Increased fat stranding of between pes anserinus near the tibial insertion and mild increased intensity inside, R/O grade 1-2 strain.
> Muscle edema at popliteus muscle and plantaris muscle and soleus muscle and increase intermuscular fat stranding, most due to trauma.

Impression: 
1. Tear of anterior cruciate ligament.
2. Bone contusion in posterior asepct of tibial plateau; the possibility of occult subchondral fracture can't excluded.
3. R/O grade 1-2 strain of pes anserinus and grade 1 MCL injury.
4. In favor of degeneration of meniscus.
5. Massive joint effusion
6. Degeneration of knee joint and grade 2-3 patellar chondromalacia.
7. Muscle strain at posterior aspect of proximal leg and subcutaneous edema around knee.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation

An at least high-grade partial disruption of the proximal and midportions of the anterior cruciate ligament is noted, some fibers are apparently continuous. 
There is an associated significant joint effusion with suprapatellar extension. No intra-articular loose bodies. 

No associated osteochondral impaction injury, well-preserved posterior cruciate and both collateral ligaments, distal iliotibial band, both menisci, no posterolateral corner injury pattern is appreciated. No fracture or marrow infiltration. There is however an element of posterior capsular disruption as evidenced by the presence of ill-defined fluid in an extra-articular location at the level of the distal femoral supracondylar region. No associated anterior tibial translation. No other finding of note.  
Impression: Appearances are in keeping with a hyperextension mechanism of injury. Arthroscopy needed to evaluate the exact extent of ACL injury.
